### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **62** documentable anchor(s).

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0e8f441a34f944d3d1acb079af216849d08dbaf8` — the merge of head `6fc6664eedda467e1cd164e86c5fcbc7ab771fd0` into base `36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0e8f441a34f944d3d1acb079af216849d08dbaf8 && git checkout 0e8f441a34f944d3d1acb079af216849d08dbaf8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802 6fc6664eedda467e1cd164e86c5fcbc7ab771fd0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802 && git merge --no-ff 6fc6664eedda467e1cd164e86c5fcbc7ab771fd0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS (L1; the contract record is review#2's)

Head-sha: `6fc6664eedda467e1cd164e86c5fcbc7ab771fd0`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-16T04:06Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `dfb8ed35` (7 files, +573/−6, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM
Ruling implemented: option A on the card's decision («服务端按托管裁剪并拒绝», edits E1–E5) · dev report 6906008980

**Contract face:** a declared narrowing, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. review#2 claimed the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record at this head (6906933086). When that record is a PASS, this read adopts it and no second record is made. Landing waits on it.

**What holds**

- **One table, every door.** `CLOUD_MANAGED_HIDDEN_SETTINGS` is read by every door: the list, the namespace read (manifest, values and `live`), the write, the actions, and the data-API read door. Every rule returns `undefined` unless `isCloudManaged()`, so a self-hosted process takes exactly the old path, and every door is driven both ways in the pins.
- **The route inventory is complete.** The settings router mounts six routes. The four namespace routes each ask the table. The two `deployment/notice` routes carry no storage or AI value.
- **The write is refused whole.** `assertWriteServed` runs on the body's keys before the echoed-mask drop and before anything is applied. The pin writes a hidden key beside a served one and asserts that neither lands, with `details.keys` naming only the hidden one.
- **The key set is closed.** The `ai` hidden list and the served complement are pinned to cover every manifest key exactly once. A provider key added later turns that pin red instead of being served by default.
- **The data-API rows match the routes.** For a non-system caller the read door ANDs in `namespace $nin [storage]` and, for `ai`, `namespace $nin [ai] OR key $nin [hidden]`, on all four objects. Both audit objects carry `namespace` and `key`, so the predicate applies to them as written. A system context reads every row, which keeps the in-process storage and AI readers whole. That is pinned too.
- **Registry whole.** The storage service's `getNamespace('storage')` and the AI service's reads are untouched, so the hosted platform's own configuration keeps working.
- **Setup entry.** `visible: 'features.cloudManaged != true'` is the same hide-when-on predicate the invitation actions carry, on the `/auth/config` flag.
- **The refusal shape** is `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with `details.managedBy: 'platform'`, the same as the other cloud-managed doors. A console can tell it apart from `404 UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE`.

**`ai.reset` in the refused set: agreed.** The manifest says `reset` "clears every saved row in this namespace", so on a hosted process it would delete the hidden rows the platform configured. That is a write to the hidden keys by another door, the same thing the PUT refuses whole. A served-keys-only reset would be a new action and outside this ruling. An administrator can still rewrite the four served keys by PUT. The refused button is also taken out of the served manifest, so the page does not offer what the door refuses.

**The battery.** 8 of 4016 were red, in 4 files that never set `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED`, and each is reported green when run alone at this head. That is the same reading I accepted on #34082, so I accept it here. Note that CI's `Dogfood Regression Gate` success on this head is the aggregate over a shard matrix that `pull_request` runs skip, not a battery result. The shards run in the merge queue.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

1. The hosted row scope is pinned on `sys_setting` and `sys_platform_setting` only. One row on each audit object would pin the two objects the changeset also names.
2. `nav_settings_storage` is not listed in `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.cloudManaged.gatedInputs`. That ledger holds object actions today, so this may fall outside its shape. Book it there if a reader of that ledger is meant to see nav entries too.
3. The namespace read refuses `storage` before the authorization read, so a caller without the settings capability learns that the environment is cloud-managed. `/auth/config` already serves that flag to everyone, so nothing new is disclosed.

**Gates:** the latest run of each check is green: 33 success, 18 skipped, none red or pending. The two earlier `PR-body guards` failures (02:38Z, 03:01Z) were superseded by the 03:10Z success.

**Can land once review#2's record at this head is a PASS.**

Read at 2026-11-16T04:11Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6906933086; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for domain:server#5; reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The ruling is implemented as ruled.** Option A (server-side trim and refuse) and its route E1 to E5 from claim 6902019399: a door check with the registry left whole, the house refusal with no code minted, one table asked at every ruled door, `ai` hidden per key, a write naming a hidden key refused whole. Each is present in the diff and none is exceeded.
- **One predicate.** Every check goes through `cloudManagedRule` or `cloudManagedRowScope`, and both read `isCloudManaged()` from `@objectstack/core` and nothing else. No second reading of the environment, no request-derived input.
- **The hidden table is exactly the ruled set.** Read against `ai.manifest.ts` at this head: the 31 hidden `ai` keys are every provider, per-provider model, credential, base-URL and account key, the three generation defaults and the six `embedder_*` keys; the four served keys are the conversation-title pair and the observability pair. Nothing of titles or observability is hidden; no provider, credential, model or Embedder key is left served. `storage` is hidden whole, with every action, the built-in `reset` included. `ai/reset` is refused beyond the three named actions because it clears hidden rows; that is inside the ruling's intent, and the PR says so.
- **Door census, settings routes.** The family mounts six routes. List: projected. Namespace read: whole-hidden refused first, then manifest, values and `live` each projected. Write: asserted after the body envelope is unwrapped and before anything is applied, so the answer does not depend on which accepted body shape names the key. Actions: asserted before the handler runs. The two deployment-notice routes carry no settings value. The write route answers only the keys it was sent, and the service's whole-state validation speaks only about touched keys, so a served-only write does not report a hidden key.
- **Door census, data API.** The four settings stores expose read only, and the read door ANDs the hosted row scope into every read verb for a non-system caller; a system context reads all rows. Reads that arrive by REST, MCP or batch reach the same engine seam.
- **In-process readers are unaffected.** `settings-service.ts` is not in the diff. The storage service's `getNamespace('storage')` and the AI readers call the service directly and are served every value; pinned on both postures.
- **Self-hosted is unchanged.** With the predicate false, every helper returns its input or `null`. Each hosted case has a self-hosted control on the same composition.
- **Sibling PR #34223 (knowledge / Embedder).** Read at its current head: it keeps the `embedder_*` key names and `test_embedder` inside the `ai` namespace, contributed by the knowledge service where mounted. This table names all of them, so the hosted table governs whichever lands first, and the classification pin stays green after the split because it does not require a hidden key to be declared. The two nav hunks touch different entries.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, same wording of what narrows; honest: hosted callers lose served answers, self-hosted callers lose nothing.
- **BREAKING** marker present with a what-to-do sentence. Changeset `patch` on `@objectstack/service-settings` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`; the no-major gate reads it as the narrowing arm at patch and is green.
- ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: correct, no schema key, accepted value or stored row changes.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct, no spec file in the diff; the nav entry uses the `features` root that `app.zod.ts` already declares for a navigation entry's `visible`.
- `Skills-docs: none` with its reason: accepted; no skill teaches these pages.
- No error code minted; `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` already exists, no ledger change needed.
- **CI at this head: 59 check-runs, all completed. 37 success, 20 skipped, 2 failure.** Both failures are earlier runs of `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, from before the claim was re-posted with the PR's own branch; the same guard also has a success run on this head. Nothing is still running. The seat should confirm the newest run of that guard is the green one before landing.

CI completed before posting: 59 check-runs on this head, 37 success, 20 skipped, 2 failure — both are superseded earlier runs of PR-body guards; the newest run of that guard on this head is a success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path and no published schema in the seven files: the path reading decides no face, and the review is owed by the narrowing declaration alone. No Tier H path. No `ui/**` path; the "managed by the platform" console page is correctly left to a ui follow-up card the seat files.
- The read door's hosted scope applies to the four settings stores. Other packages' read surfaces are outside this PR's file surface and outside the ruled door list; see S1.
- A caller of a hosted environment that lacks the settings capability now meets the hosted answer before the permission answer on the refused doors. It states only what the public table states.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published contract on `main`: it takes a served answer away only where the runtime declares itself cloud-managed, which is the ruled outcome, and it makes the refusal the house cloud-managed answer that a console can tell apart from an unknown namespace. A door check instead of a registry withholding is the right shape, because the readers that stay live under hosted read the registry. The table is small, frozen, and the one place to change.

- S1 (should-fix) — the door census is closed for the ruled doors, not for every reader of settings history. The hosted table is asked at the settings routes and the four settings stores; whether the platform's other records of a settings change ask it is neither changed nor pinned here. No credential value is served anywhere I read. This wants a carrier card in the owning lane before any doc states that a hosted environment never shows these settings; detail is with the seat.
- S2 (should-fix) — the write door's refusal is pinned for one accepted body shape only. The code is correct for both at this head; add a hosted case for the other accepted shape so the order of the check cannot regress silently.
- N1 (nit) — `ai` hides by naming keys and actions, so anything not named is served. The classification pin walks the bundled manifest's keys; it does not walk action ids, nor specifiers another package contributes to `ai` at run time. Consider classifying action ids in the same pin.
- N2 (nit) — the hosted cases in the read-door pin cover the two stores, not their two audit objects; they ride the same seam, one case each would say so.
- N3 (nit) — the projected `ai` page keeps its namespace description, which still speaks of provider, credentials and host-installed packages; the nav label stays "AI & Embedder". Copy for the ui follow-up.
- N4 (nit) — the `live` projection has no test leg, as the PR states; acceptable while nothing registers one for `ai` in this repository.

No must-fix.
